2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.

p.seg: In ancient times, when Róngchéngshì,
...... [ ] Zūn Lúshì, Hèxūshì, [ ]
Gāoxīnshì, Cāngjiéshì,
Xuānyuánshì, Shénnóngshì,
Húndūnshì, and Fúxīshì possessed the world,
none passed it to their sons
but instead passed it to the worthy.
Their virtue was pure and clear,
those above loved those below,
and unified their will,
laying aside their weapons,
and appointing officials according to their talents.
Thus, the mute and deaf held torches,
the blind and dim-sighted played the se,
the lame and crippled guarded gates,
dwarves made arrows,
the hunchbacked divined for dwellings,
the bent-over managed calculations,
the goitered boiled salt for dwellings,
the bald fished in marshes,
... the disabled and abandoned were not [ ]
All common people of low status,
they taught and instructed them,
gave them drink and food,
and employed them in the hundred offices,
providing them monthly provisions.
Therefore, at that time,
... there was no annexation [ ]
... [ ]shì possessed the world,
showing deep love
and light taxation,
exerting their own strength to labor for the people.
... [ ] Thus, there was no rewarding or punishing,
no penalizing or killing,
the state had no starving people,
and on the roads, no one died prematurely.
Those above and below, noble and base,
each occupied their proper place.
Beyond the Four Seas, all were guests,
within the Four Seas, all were upright.
Birds and beasts paid court,
fish and turtles offered tribute,
and there was exchange between having and not having.
He rectified the governance of the world for nineteen years,
and ruled the world as king for thirty-seven years,
then vanished (?) in the end.
In ancient times, Yáo dwelled between Dānfǔ and Diàolíng.
Yáo trod the path and timely sacrificed,
without urging, the people exerted their strength;
without penalizing or killing, there were no thieves or robbers.
Extremely lenient, yet the people submitted.
Thus, within a hundred li square,
he led the people of the world,
who came to serve and establish him,
making him the Son of Heaven.
Thus, within a thousand li square,
[thus] holding the tablet and rectifying his position,
harmonizing in all four directions,
he embraced to attract the people of the world.
His governance was orderly without rewards,
officials were appointed without conferring ranks,
without driving the people,
yet he governed disorder without weariness.
Therefore it is said:
... worthy and reaching [ ]
Thus, to regard the worthy:
treading the earth and bearing the sky,
steadfast in righteousness and trustworthiness,
meeting between heaven and earth,
and encompassing within the Four Seas,
fully capable in their tasks,
and establishing them as Son of Heaven.
Yáo taught them, saying:
"Examine yourselves inwardly,
and I will observe through a crevice,
seeking the worthy,
and yielding to the worthy."
Yáo offered the world to the worthy,
but the worthy of the world
were unable to accept it.
The lords of the ten thousand states
all offered their states to the worthy.
... [ ] the worthy,
yet the worthy were unable to accept it.
Thus, the people of the world,
regarding Yáo as good at promoting the worthy,
finally established him.
In ancient times, Shùn plowed at Lìqiū,
made pottery by the riverbank,
fished at Léizé,
filially cared for his parents,
treating his kin well,
and extended this to the sons of the state.
Yáo heard of this,
and praised his conduct.
Yáo then prepared fifteen chariots,
and with three, followed Shùn into the fields.
Shùn then first set aside his sickle, hoe, and spade,
and sat between them.
Yáo faced south,
Shùn faced north.
Shùn then first spoke to Yáo
about the ways of heaven, earth, and the people.
Speaking with him about governance,
he was pleased with its simplicity in practice;
speaking with him about music,
he was pleased with its harmony and expansiveness;
speaking with him about rites,
he was pleased with their breadth and lack of opposition.
Yáo then was pleased.
Yáo [then aged,
his sight unclear],
his hearing not sharp.
Yáo had nine sons,
but did not make his son his successor.
Seeing Shùn's worthiness,
he wished to make him his successor.
[Shùn then five times yielded to the worthy of the world,
and only when unavoidable,
dared he accept it.]
Shùn attended to governance for three years,
mountains and hills were not neglected,
floodwaters were not stagnant,
and he then appointed Yǔ as Minister of Works.
Yǔ, having received the command,
then wore garments of grass and bamboo-leaf hats,
...... lotus plants [ ] pair [ ]
... [ ] face parched and rough,
shins without growing hair,
opening blockages and clearing streams.
Yǔ personally held basket and spade,
to embank the marsh of Míngdū (=Mèngzhū),
breaching the obstacles of the nine rivers,
thus making Jiázhōu and Xúzhōu begin to be habitable.
Yǔ connected the Huái and Yí rivers,
channeling them east into the sea,
thus making Qīngzhōu and Jǔzhōu begin to be habitable.
Yǔ then connected the Lóu and Tāng rivers,
channeling them east into the sea,
thus making Yōuzhōu begin to be habitable.
Yǔ then connected the Three Jiangs and Five Lakes,
channeling them east into the sea, thus making Jīngzhōu and Yángzhōu begin to be habitable.
Yǔ then connected the Yī and Luò, joining the Chán and Jiàn,
channeling them east into the Hé,
thus making Yùzhōu begin to be habitable.
Yǔ then connected the Jīng and Wèi,
channeling them north into the Hé,
thus making Yōngzhōu begin to be habitable.
Yǔ then from the Hàn river southward made five hundred named valleys,
from the Hàn river northward made five hundred named valleys.
The people of the world settled in dwellings,
then plowed (?) for food,
and then appointed Hòujì as Overseer.
Hòujì, having received the command,
then ate in the wilds,
lodged in the wilds,
restored grain and nurtured the soil,
and after five years, there was abundance.
The people had surplus food,
with no desires unmet,
and the people then made offerings.
Arrogance and indulgence began to arise,
and then Gāoyáo was appointed as Judge.
Gāoyáo, having received the command,
then distinguished the yīn and yáng energies,
and heard lawsuits and disputes.
After three years, there were no people in the world involved in lawsuits or disputes.
The world was greatly harmonious and balanced,
and Shùn then wished to gather the energies of heaven and earth
and employ them in governance,
and then appointed Zhì as Music Director.
Zhì, having received the command, created the six pitch-standards and six pitch-pipes,
distinguishing the five notes,
to fix the sounds of men and women.
At that time,
epidemics did not come,
portents and omens did not occur,
calamities and disasters departed and vanished,
birds and beasts grew large and fat,
and plants and trees flourished and grew.
In ancient times, heaven and earth assisted Shùn
and aided the good,
in such manner.
Shùn then aged,
his sight unclear,
his hearing not sharp.
Shùn had seven sons,
but did not make his son his successor.
Seeing Yǔ's worthiness,
he wished to make him his successor.
Yǔ then five times yielded to the worthy of the world,
and only when unavoidable,
dared he accept it.
After Yǔ assumed governance for three years,
he did not make leather armor,
did not sharpen metal weapons,
did not fletch arrows,
the fields had no weeds,
houses were not empty,
and at the passes and markets there were no taxes.
Yǔ then, based on the hills, mounds, and level lowlands suitable for establishing settlements,
populated and enriched them;
he used the near to understand the distant,
abolished harshness and practiced simplicity,
followed the desires of the people,
and harmonized with the benefits of Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, those nearby delighted in his governance,
and those far away came of their own accord.
Within the Four Seas and
beyond the Four Seas, all requested to offer tribute.
Yǔ then for the first time created signal flags,
to distinguish left and right,
so that the people would not be confused.
The flag for the east bore the sun,
the flag for the west bore the moon,
the flag for the south bore a snake,
the central and correct flag bore a bear,
and the flag for the north bore a bird.
Yǔ then began to practice frugality:
his clothing was not brightly beautiful,
his food was not of multiple flavors,
at court he did not use carriages to receive guests,
in spring he did not hull rice finely,
and when butchering he did not break bones.
He established the principle of filial piety (??),
and made the three proclamations,
to save the records of sounds:
in the east were the three proclamations,
in the west were the three proclamations,
in the south were the three proclamations,
in the north were the three proclamations,
to guard the ravines and valleys,
cross the broad rivers,
ascend the high mountains,
enter the dense forests,
and thereby administer governance.
Then for the first time he conferred ranks and distributed emoluments,
yielding to those who came,
reverently and harmoniously,
saying, "Virtue quickly urges ???"
.... [ ] surface skin exclusively?
Yǔ then set up a drum in the court,
so that those among the people who had lawsuits or complaints would strike it.
When the drum was struck,
Yǔ would certainly come out quickly,
in winter not daring to use cold as an excuse,
in summer not daring to use heat as an excuse.
He personally spoke [and taught by personal example]
.... [ ] abyss place
It is said:
"The sage,
during his life bestows nurture,
upon his death bestows burial,
removes harshness and wickedness,
and thereby gains fame."
Yǔ had five sons.
He did not make his own son his successor,
seeing the worthiness of Gāo Yáo,
and wishing to make him the successor.
Gāo Yáo then five times yielded to the worthy ones of the world,
and finally pleaded illness
and did not come out, then died.
Yǔ then yielded to Yì,
but Qǐ then attacked Yì and took it for himself.
[Qǐ] ruled the world for sixteen years,
and then Jié arose.
Jié did not follow the Way of his former kings,
.... he himself changed it [altered it] [ ]
... [ ] At that time,
the strong and weak did not decline to hear cases,
the many and few did not listen to lawsuits,
and the affairs of Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons were not put in order.
Tāng then broadly implemented registration for conscription,
to levy taxes at passes and markets.
The people then became resentful,
cruel diseases began to arise,
and then there emerged the mute, deaf, lame, blind, goitrous, hunchbacked, who began to appear.
Tāng then planned caution and sought worthies,
and established Yī Yǐn as his assistant.
After Yī Yǐn had received the mandate,
he took up arms to prohibit violence.
Pretending to gain favor with the people,
he then became deluded,
and without considering that his strength was insufficient,
raised an army to attack the Mínshān clan,
taking their two daughters Yǎn and Wǎn,
and taking them north away from their state,
[ ] built a leaning palace,
constructed a jade chamber,
adorned a jade terrace,
and erected a jade gate.
His arrogance and excess were like this.
Tāng heard of it,
and then cautiously warned and sought worthies.
He bestowed virtue and kindness but did not rely on it,
accumulating for thirty years.
And he was capable of it.
If even this was not acceptable,
then afterwards he would attack them.
Ascending from the Róng (Ér?) pass,
entering from the north gate,
.. standing in the center [ ]
Jié then fled to the Lìshān clan.
Tāng again followed and attacked him,
descending from the Míngtiáo pass,
to attack the gate of Gāoshén.
Jié then fled to the Náncháo clan.
Tāng again followed and attacked him,
and he fled,
going to the wilderness of Cāngwú.
Tāng then summoned the armies of the Nine Provinces,
to pacify within the Four Seas.
Then the armies of the world rose up greatly,
then ancestral lines perished,
clans were slaughtered,
groups were mutilated,
and they submitted.
... [ ] thieves and robbers,
and thereby he gained the multitude
and ruled the world.
King Tāng ruled the world for thirty-one generations,
and then Zhòu arose.
Zhòu did not follow the Way of his former kings,
he himself altered and changed,
then built a nine-story tower,
placed basins of charcoal beneath it,
placed round logs above them,
and made people tread on them.
Those who could cross, crossed;
those who could not cross
fell in and died.
Those who did not obey orders were then put in shackles and fetters.
Then he made three thousand metal shackles.
After making the metal shackles,
he also made a pool of wine,
indulging deeply in the pleasure of wine.
Day and night he engaged in debauchery,
and did not attend to the governance of his state.
Then nine states rebelled against him:
Fēng, Hào, Zhōu, Shíyì, Yú, Lù, Lí, Chóng, and Mìxūshì.
King Wén heard of it,
and said:
"Even if the ruler lacks the Way,
how dare a minister not serve him?
Even if a father lacks the Way,
how dare a son not serve him?
Who, being the Son of Heaven, can be opposed?"
Zhòu heard of it,
and then released King Wén from beneath the Xiàtái
and asked him,
saying:
"Can the nine states be made to come?"
King Wén said:
"They can."
X King Wén then, in plain mourning garments (??),
went to the nine states,
and seven states came and submitted.
Fēng and Hào did not submit.
King Wén then raised an army and marched toward Fēng and Hào.
He drummed three times
and advanced against them,
drummed three times
and withdrew from them,
saying:
"What I know is that many are pitiable;
one man is without the Way,
what crime do the common people have?"
The people of Fēng and Hào heard this,
and then surrendered to King Wén.
King Wén held to the old seasons
and taught the people the seasons,
fully knowing the benefits of high and low, fertile and barren land,
knowing the Way of Heaven,
knowing the benefits of Earth,
and making the people not suffer.
In the past, when King Wén assisted Zhòu,
it was like this.
King Wén passed away,
and King Wǔ ascended the throne.
King Wǔ said:
"Those who have perfected virtue,
I am pleased and will replace them.
Those next to them,
I will attack and replace them.
Now Zhòu acts without the Way,
exterminating and discarding the common people,
shackling and constraining the feudal lords.
Heaven will punish him,
and I will assist Heaven's majesty."
King Wǔ thereupon made a thousand war chariots,
equipped ten thousand armored soldiers,
and on the day of Wùwǔ,
crossed at Mèngjīn,
reaching the area between Gòng and Téng,
where he briefly met with the armies of the feudal lords on the plain of Mùyě.
